import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class B {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        PrintWriter pw = new PrintWriter(System.out);

        String[] input = br.readLine().split("\\s+");
        int N = Integer.parseInt(input[0]);
        double P = Double.parseDouble(input[1]);

        int result = 0;
        // Try each possible number of maps to study (from 0 to N)
        for (int studied = 0; studied <= N; studied++) {
            double prob = calculateProbability(N, studied);
            if (prob >= P) {
                result = studied;
                break;
            }
        }

        pw.println(result);
        pw.close();
    }

    // Calculate probability that a studied map is selected given N total maps and 'studied' maps studied
    private static double calculateProbability(int N, int studied) {
        // Total ways to choose 3 maps from N
        long totalWays = (long) N * (N - 1) * (N - 2) / 6;

        // Count favorable cases where at least one of the 3 shown maps is studied
        // and that studied map is selected (either both players discard others, or system picks it)

        // Better approach: calculate probability directly
        // Case 1: 0 studied maps in the 3 shown
        // Case 2: 1 studied map in the 3 shown
        // Case 3: 2 studied maps in the 3 shown
        // Case 4: 3 studied maps in the 3 shown

        double prob = 0.0;

        // Probability of k studied maps in the 3 shown
        for (int k = 0; k <= Math.min(3, studied); k++) {
            if (k > 3 || N - studied < 3 - k) continue;

            long waysToChooseKStudied = comb(studied, k);
            long waysToChooseNonStudied = comb(N - studied, 3 - k);
            long favorableWays = waysToChooseKStudied * waysToChooseNonStudied;

            double probGivenK = 0.0;

            if (k == 0) {
                probGivenK = 0.0; // no studied maps shown
            } else if (k == 1) {
                // 1 studied map, 2 unstudied
                // Each player picks one to discard randomly
                // System picks randomly from maps not discarded by anyone
                // If both players discard the same unstudied map, system picks the studied one
                // If players discard different unstudied maps, system picks the studied one
                // If one discards studied and other discards unstudied, system picks the remaining unstudied
                // Let's enumerate:
                // Maps: S (studied), U1, U2 (unstudied)
                // Player1 choices: S, U1, U2
                // Player2 choices: S, U1, U2
                // System picks from maps not chosen by either player
                // Favorable: system picks S
                // This happens when both players discard U1 and U2 (in any order)
                // Player1 discards U1, Player2 discards U2 -> system picks S
                // Player1 discards U2, Player2 discards U1 -> system picks S
                // So 2 favorable out of 9 total combinations
                probGivenK = 2.0 / 9.0;
            } else if (k == 2) {
                // 2 studied maps S1, S2, 1 unstudied U
                // Favorable: system picks at least one studied map
                // System picks from maps not discarded by anyone
                // For system to pick a studied map, at least one studied map must not be discarded by either player
                // Let's enumerate: players each choose one of 3 maps to discard
                // Total: 9 combinations
                // Favorable cases: system picks S1 or S2
                // System picks S1 if neither player discards S1
                // System picks S2 if neither player discards S2
                // System picks U if neither player discards U
                // Cases where system picks S1: both players don't discard S1
                //   Player1 discards S2 or U, Player2 discards S2 or U
                //   But if both discard same map, system picks from remaining 2
                // Let's be more careful:
                // Maps: S1, S2, U
                // Player choices (discard):
                // (S1,S1): system picks from {S2, U} randomly -> 0.5 chance studied
                // (S1,S2): system picks from {U} -> 0 chance studied
                // (S1,U): system picks from {S2} -> 1 chance studied
                // (S2,S1): system picks from {U} -> 0 chance studied
                // (S2,S2): system picks from {S1, U} randomly -> 0.5 chance studied
                // (S2,U): system picks from {S1} -> 1 chance studied
                // (U,S1): system picks from {S2} -> 1 chance studied
                // (U,S2): system picks from {S1} -> 1 chance studied
                // (U,U): system picks from {S1, S2} randomly -> 1 chance studied
                // Count favorable: (S1,S1):0.5, (S1,U):1, (S2,S2):0.5, (S2,U):1, (U,S1):1, (U,S2):1, (U,U):1
                // That's 7 cases with probabilities: 0.5+1+0.5+1+1+1+1 = 6 out of 9 total combinations
                // But wait, we need to count each combination equally (9 total)
                // Favorable probability = (0.5 + 0 + 1 + 0 + 0.5 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1) / 9 = 6/9 = 2/3
                probGivenK = 6.0 / 9.0;
            } else if (k == 3) {
                // All 3 maps studied
                // System will always pick a studied map
                probGivenK = 1.0;
            }

            prob += (double) favorableWays / totalWays * probGivenK;
        }

        return prob;
    }

    // Calculate combination C(n, k)
    private static long comb(int n, int k) {
        if (k < 0 || k > n) return 0;
        if (k == 0 || k == n) return 1;

        long result = 1;
        for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
            result = result * (n - i) / (i + 1);
        }
        return result;
    }
}
